findings.location: REVIEW-OUTCOME.md section 6 route C (lines 164-187) and recommendation (lines 203-208); OUTCOME.json routes_for_owner[C].substitutes and recommendation
findings.summary: Route C's substitution omits two contract terms that must change on Darwin. First, the original supervisor: P05 CONTRACT.md sections 3 and 7 require it (calling the original supervisor.run_process exactly once; 'Preserve the original Python run_process'), and P07 uses it for H1. It is Linux-only: supervisor.py lines 171-173 call prctl PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER and otherwise raise 'Cannot establish Linux descendant reaping'. Second, the Linux host bindings of the provider and probe (Linux platform, procfs boot id, ldd role, ELF interpreter, Linux Node pin, linux-cp312 lock). Route C still lists 'exactly three real checkers' as unchanged. Add these terms to the route's substitutes, add the lost subreaper guarantee to the claims route C can never support, and restate the recommendation's basis.

findings.location: EXECUTOR-INVENTORY.json host and executors; REVIEW-OUTCOME.md section 3
findings.summary: Some executor classes are not inventoried. Node executables bundled in apps, all Mach-O arm64: application A's bundled node 24.14.0, application B's bundled node 24.22.3-cua.1, application C's helper node, and Node embedded through Electron. Other Python interpreters: uv-managed CPython 3.12.11 and 3.11.14, and /usr/bin/python3. Remote agent sandboxes, which are of X4's kind and not local. The OS's own virtualization and Rosetta for Linux, with no VM manager installed. None changes a verdict.

findings.location: OUTCOME.json preparation_dispositions[3]; REVIEW-OUTCOME.md section 3 X2, section 5 row 4, section 6
findings.summary: The VM reason covers only an emulated amd64 guest. An arm64 glibc Linux guest would run under native virtualization. It would keep Linux and the original supervisor's subreaper, but fail the x86-64 pins and profiles (E4-E7) and need installed tooling and a profile decision. State it as a route or record why it is excluded.

findings.location: REVIEW-OUTCOME.md section 3 (lines 101-105), section 6 route C (lines 185-187), recommendation (lines 205-206); OUTCOME.json recommendation
findings.summary: The branch driver resolves the selection before the workspace copy and every step, so after R04 the whole local routine on the Mac would refuse to start, not only the unit stage. 'The integration gate needs [route C] in any case' is too strong: route C or another reviewed amendment of the selection rule would serve. Route D also needs no new machine and no change of mode.

findings.location: EXECUTOR-INVENTORY.json X1, X3, X5; REVIEW-OUTCOME.md section 3
findings.summary: X3's facts about GitHub's runners were not observed and should be labelled inference; E7 may also be unmet. X5's statement that the startup report asked about a Linux machine is in no record. X1 lists E8 as unmet without a reason (C.UTF-8 exists on macOS). The Markdown says X1 fails E1-E8 while the JSON omits E3. Saying the inspector refuses X1 at its 'first host check' misstates the order: for /0.1.1 and later plans, _check_author_runtime (line 3011) runs before _check_host_static (line 3013).

The records list /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu as absent, but the bound raw output EXECUTORS.txt (74ee47e5) observed /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu instead. The path is in fact absent, as observed again by this review, but the record should cite what its raw evidence shows.

findings.location: READ-SET.json state_at_declaration; outcome records; REVIEW-OUTCOME.md header; inputs_identical_to fields
findings.summary: READ-SET promises that the outcome records list later inputs and the entries opened. They do not, and the outcome cites 8 inputs without identities, listed in REVIEW.md. The named h0-plan-p21, p23 and p26 directories (59, 187 and 22 files) are bound only by 2, 1 and 3 files. 'Every input is byte-identical to 4ee55b03' is untrue for the four workflow records that the declaration updated; the fields the outcome relies on are unchanged.

A2 omits some H0/H1 requirements: the seven package metadata pins, the exact -I -S -B launcher with its exact environment, the preparer's installation receipts, the outer capture descriptors, the admitted Git closure and H1's use of the original supervisor. E1's line range is 1202-1221. No verdict changes, because E1 fails first.

'A changed Codex runtime would itself stop the plan (E2, E4)': E2's Node comes from the retained Library archive installed in a task-specific directory, not from the Codex runtime. Say E4, and E5-E7 if the host image changes.
